It can be both a good and a bad thing. Letting go of your emotions is a sign of maturity: when you're a kid if someone calls you ugly-face you get really pissed off and there's nothing you can do about. it. When you're an adult you know better than to get mad at someone who is deliberately trying to get you mad gratuitously - or even about becoming mad over little things.

But if you just let go of your emotions all the time then you can be made a puppet, or even worse, lose your identity - values, morals, etc. So how to solve this dilemma? The quick answer is the only motto you'll ever need: balance in all things, but me telling you to achieve balance in all the things is not that helpful/easy to do either (but something to think about dearly nonetheless).

So here is a more practical advice: never take other people's crap for yourself. You don't have to punch your "agressor" in the face to make a stand but something as simple as saying NO, without any other excuses or explanations is sometimes enough to stand your ground. Other times you may not reply but instead deal with it by making plans to avoid the same situation in the future. So basically: never ever let the ball settle in your court. You can throw the ball back or you can hold it for a while and pass it on, you can explode the ball, you can throw it away to no-one. Just don't let something sink in that is not yours to bear. Do something, anything, however big or small but don't let go of you dignity when simply saying NO is often just enough to let people know you're not OK with a bad situation.

BWE

  • Character progression is not wiped so you can still work on your masteries in beta weekend 2 etc

Mastery Points

  • Each of the story instances in Living World Season 2 will grant you 1 Mastery point each retroactively. This is to give a legs up for the experienced players.

Pact Commander Mastery

  • Pact Mentor – Unlocks a special mentoring badge (purple star shown in PoI is a placeholder see this comment), accessible from the party menu. You will also display a new chat title (shows mentor next to your name in chat) when this is active. In cities, you and your party gain 5% swiftness (does not stack with regular swiftness). You can turn the mentoring mode on/off in the party menu. Does not work in WvW and does not allow you to create squads.

  • Productive Downtime – Gain bonus crafting XP, raising your crafting skills more quickly for each item crafted.

  • Supply Line Management – Gain access to a network of regional merchants across Tyria with rare goods for trade (old or rare recipes for example, also new recipes such as the recipe for a new Melandru backpack. Recipes will be tradeable). The merchant will use Karma as its currency. Your city-wide swiftness boost raises to 15%.
  • Noblesse Oblige – Increased revive speed depending on the level difference of the player you are reviving. This also takes away a stack of downed penalty and armor damage.
  • Advanced Logistics – You will automatically pick up nearby loot from fallen foes (this is different from auto-loot. You do not need to hit any buttons to loot with this active). This feature works even if you are dead as long you tag the enemy and does not work for chests/gadgets. Your City-wide swiftness boost raises to 33%.
    • More info on the Advanced Logistics from /u/ArenaNetRyanD:

> I can clarify this a bit. If you waypoint away before something dies and it dropped loot, you won't immediately get it. If you return to the area, you will get the loot as soon as you can see it. If you waypoint, the loot will spawn at your location and should get immediately picked up. If your inventory is full when something drops, it will be left on the ground and you will have to pick it up manually after you clear out some space.

Q&A

    • We have great players already ingame, a few bad players shouldn’t ruin the system. Since there is no reward associated with this, we are not encouraging any bad behavior.

    • To combat botting, we put it in a mastery line.
